components.label: Shard router

components.label: Shard maps
components.responsibility: Own key values and generations under independent shard locks.

components.label: Per-shard method lock
components.responsibility: Use one shard mutex or RW lock, never a process-wide lock for ordinary operations.

components.label: Timing wheel buckets
components.responsibility: Insert key/generation/deadline with wheel slot and remaining rounds.

components.label: Passive deadline check
components.responsibility: Check exact deadline during every get and conditionally remove an expired generation.

components.label: Bucket sweep
components.responsibility: Drain a bounded bucket segment and compare generation plus current deadline under the shard lock.

components.label: Shard budgets
components.responsibility: Bound each shard and report skew; choose explicit rejection or local eviction rather than borrowing unbounded memory.

components.label: Timer lifecycle
components.responsibility: Fence close state per shard, stop wheel scheduling and join drain tasks.

requirements.text: A get linearizes against put and never returns an entry expired at its lookup timestamp.
Expired cleanup cannot remove a newer replacement value.
Bound memory with passive lookup expiry and bounded active sweeps; define zero/negative TTL and shutdown.

problem.scope: In-process get/put/expiry design with an injected monotonic clock. Compare a read/write-locked map plus expiry heap with sharded maps plus timing wheels. Shared read locks permit concurrent readers but are not lock-free.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

acceptanceCases.given: A key has value A expiring at 10.
acceptanceCases.then: Return A before 10 and absence at 10.
acceptanceCases.when: Read at 9 and 10 with an injected monotonic clock.

acceptanceCases.given: A timer references generation 1 but put installed generation 2.
acceptanceCases.then: Retain generation 2 and remove only the matching expired generation.

evidence.testName: TTL exact deadline and generation checks preserve fresh replacement

acceptanceCases.given: An old entry expires at 10 and a replacement at 29.
acceptanceCases.then: Return absence at expiry and preserve the newer generation from stale cleanup.
acceptanceCases.when: Read at the exact boundary and invoke stale generation cleanup.

guarantees: An old heap record does not authorize deleting a replacement.
A newer put survives a stale reader cleanup.
Sweep work per tick is bounded; backlog remains observable.
TTL is not a memory-capacity policy.
No background task retains the cache after close returns.
